{{Short description|German chemist (1929–2020)}}
'''Dietmar Seyferth''' (January 11, 1929 &ndash; June 6, 2020) was an emeritus professor of chemistry at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].  He published widely on topics in [[organometallic chemistry]] and was the founding editor of the journal ''[[Organometallics]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Seyferth | first1 = Dietmar | year = 2010 | title = Looking Back on Happy Years in Chemistry | journal = Organometallics | volume = 29 | issue = 21| pages = 4648–4681 | doi = 10.1021/om100948g }}</ref>

==Biography==
Seyferth was born in 1929 in [[Chemnitz]], [[Free State of Saxony|Saxony]], [[Weimar Republic|Germany]], and received his college education at the [[University of Buffalo]]. His PhD thesis, which focused on [[Main-group element|main group]] chemistry was completed under the mentorship of [[Eugene G. Rochow]] at [[Harvard University|Harvard]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gingold | first1 = K. | last2 = Rochow | first2 = E. G. | last3 = Seyferth | first3 = D. | last4 = Smith | first4 = Jr. | last5 = West | first5 = R. | year = 1952 | title = Ionization of Organometallic Halides | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | volume = 74 | issue = 24 | page = 6306 | doi=10.1021/ja01144a532}}</ref>  Seyferth spent his entire academic career at {{abbr|MIT|Massachusetts Institute of Technology}}, where he initially concentrated on [[organophosphorus]], [[organosilicon]], and [[organomercury chemistry]].  He also contributed to [[organocobalt chemistry]] and [[organoiron chemistry]], e.g. the popularization of [[Disulfidobis(tricarbonyliron)|Fe<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>(CO)<sub>6</sub>]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Seyferth | first1 = D. | last2 = Henderson | first2 = R. S. | last3 = Gallagher | first3 = M. K. | year = 1980 | title = (m-Dithio)bis(tricarbonyliron) as an organic disulfide mimic: insertion of low-valent metal species into the sulfur-sulfur bond | journal = J. Organomet. Chem. | volume = 193 | page = C75 | doi = 10.1016/S0022-328X(00)90307-3 }}</ref> He died on Saturday, June 6, 2020, due to complications from [[COVID-19]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Randall |first1=Danielle |title=Dietmar Seyferth, professor emeritus of chemistry, dies at 91 |url=https://chemistry.mit.edu/chemistry-news/dietmar-seyferth-professor-emeritus-of-chemistry-dies-at-91/ |website=MIT Chemistry |date=17 June 2020 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |access-date=17 June 2020}}</ref>

Seyferth has been widely recognized, notably with the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|American Chemical Society Award]] in Organometallic Chemistry and election to the [[National Academy of Sciences|U.S. National Academy of Sciences]].
